title: Gifts, tickets, travel and payments at an official’s request
question: What do lobbyists and their clients give officials and staff outside campaign contributions?
finding: Lobbyists reported 86 expenses for officials worth $6,256 in all since 2010, mostly event tickets and meals, plus 61 disclosures of pay to an official’s family member. Officials and staff reported 294 gifts worth $66,443 from lobbying firms and from clients then paying a lobbyist; for 38 of them the giver’s lobbyists reported contacting the same person within two years before or a year after. Lobbying clients and firms made 76 payments worth $4.7 million to third parties at an elected official’s request, and paid for 5 trips.
how: Four records are read: the “activity expense” lines on lobbyists’ monthly reports; gifts on officials’ Form 700; gifts of travel reported by elected officials; and payments made at an official’s request (Forms 3610b and 803). The last three are kept when the giver’s name matches a firm that sells lobbying, or a client that was paying a lobbyist within a year of the gift (two years for travel and requested payments). “Contacts” counts that giver’s lobbyists’ reported contacts with the recipient in the two years before and the year after. Payments at an official’s request are covered more fully in the “interests” results.
limits: Gifts within the legal limits are reported by the recipient; a payment at an official’s request goes to a charity or public purpose, not to the official. Many of the gifts are tickets to civic events given to scores of officials at once by bodies such as a business association or a museum that also lobbies. A name match can join a giver to a different client of the same name. The Form 700 file holds what officials chose to report; an unreported gift is invisible here.
